text:
Jordan Eberle is 36, in his fifth season in Seattle, and still one of the Kraken's most dependable sources of offense. Eleven points in 16 games, and seven of them on the power play, where his shot from the half wall remains a weapon.

His five goals match his 5.13 expected goals almost exactly, so there is no luck to strip out. He shoots from dangerous spots, as our comparisons put it, and does it often (36 shots).

The worry is what happens at even strength. With Eberle on the ice at 5v5, Seattle has 45% of shot attempts and 44% of expected goals, a little worse than the team without him. Some of that is the team around him, but at this stage of his career his value is concentrated on the man advantage. The last ten games brought six points, a bit below what our numbers expected.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth about one win above replacement last season, almost all of it from offense. That is the player: a finisher whose minutes are worth managing.
headline: Eberle keeps Seattle's power play honest
